comparator.name: Bachelor Aerospace Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 Implementation Regulations and currently linked pre-2027 module chart were freshly retrieved on 8 October 2026. The adopted general structure remains first-year major 60 EC, second-year major 60 EC, minor 30 EC, third-year major 15 EC and Design Synthesis Exercise 15 EC: 180. All 22 previously verified course/module components and their weights are retained unchanged. The 2022–2023 chart is the still-linked applicable pre-September-2027 structure; the September 2027 redesign is excluded from this 2026 entrant reconstruction. Wind-tunnel testing is embedded in Aerodynamics 7 EC, aerospace AI is embedded in Test, Analysis and Simulation 8 EC, and zero-credit reporting/language training does not add credits. The current public Dutch and English programme pages advertise English or Dutch–English and the Dutch page explicitly mentions a bilingual track. Normalized metadata therefore includes ENG and retains NLD; the raw NLD offering remains unchanged. This fresh content qualifies the earlier audit English-only proposal. The generic current instruction options do not establish a different 2026 curriculum, a new formal specialization, or retroactive bilingual-track applicability for the selected entrant. No future curricular units are imported.

core: Aircraft and spacecraft design, aerodynamics, flight and orbital mechanics, structures, materials, propulsion, aerospace systems and experimental verification
Calculus, linear algebra, differential equations, numerical methods, probability, data analysis and system models
Programming, artificial intelligence, optimisation, robotics, drones and autonomous decision systems
Team design, product development, systems integration, safety and engineering decision-making
adjacent: Sustainable aviation, wind-energy technology, climate mitigation, Earth systems and responsible resource use
questions: How can mathematical and computational models support safe, efficient and autonomous technological systems?
How can technology reduce the climate and resource impacts of transport and energy systems?

alternatives.label: Computational systems, autonomous technology & sustainable engineering
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by mathematics, programming, algorithms, data, optimisation, machine learning and robotics, with one product-development course and a bounded energy-and-sustainability strand. It does not claim aerospace engineering, flight mechanics, structures, propulsion or experimental testing.
alternatives.concept: Develop calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, linear systems, probability, programming, algorithms, image analysis, optimisation, machine learning, robotics and autonomous decision methods, together with product development and renewable-energy assessment. This supports aerospace-linked systems questions through related fields rather than reproducing Aerospace Engineering.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and eight 300-level courses. Programming precedes algorithms and autonomous-system work; Mathematical Methods precedes dependent mathematics, robotics and neural networks; Sustainability Essentials I precedes II and Renewable System Design. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort term.

alternatives.label: Quantitative modelling, Earth systems & renewable technology
alternatives.labelReason: Six autonomous-computing courses are replaced by Earth-system, geoscience, resource-recovery and advanced-resource courses, producing a distinct natural-system and renewable-technology curriculum while retaining mathematics, data analysis and one product-development project. The label does not imply aerospace, wind-turbine or geophysics training.
alternatives.concept: Combine mathematical and computational modelling with Earth-system science, field and laboratory investigation, water–mineral interactions, resource recovery, climate mitigation, renewable-system assessment and one product-development project. This is a sustainable-technology response to the target’s wind-energy and environmental-impact interests, not an aerospace curriculum.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and seven 300-level courses. Sustainability Essentials I precedes II and all dependent resource and energy courses; Mathematical Methods precedes later mathematics and neural-network study. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort term.
alternatives.distinctness: Six courses, or 45 EC, differ in each direction. Optimisation, networks, algorithms, robotics, AI decision-making and reinforcement learning are replaced by Earth-system modelling, Dynamic Earth, soils and aquifers, environmental biogeochemistry, resource recovery and advanced resource research. These changes implement the evidenced sustainability and wind-energy direction rather than threshold-filling substitutions.

candidates.label: Sustainable aviation, wind energy and environmental transition
Space systems, satellites and mission design
candidates.reason: UCR has no orbital or spaceflight mechanics, rocket propulsion, spacecraft systems, satellite-subsystem, mission-analysis or space-design sequence. General mathematics, AI and robotics cannot support a distinct complete space-systems curriculum.

selection.assessment: The first programme is the strongest complete related quantitative, computational, autonomous-systems and product-development response. The sustainability and wind-energy evidence supports a materially different Earth-and-renewable-technology programme, differing by six courses. A separate space-systems and mission-design direction was assessed next but cannot support a complete UCR programme without orbital mechanics, propulsion, spacecraft systems or mission design. Production stops at two alternatives.

Both establish calculus for engineering models; UCR also introduces matrices, complex numbers and differential equations.
Both directly study linear algebra, matrices, vector spaces and transformations.
Both develop numerical and computational modelling methods; UCR is not embedded in aerospace applications.

Aerospace engineering science, testing & integrated design
The 15-EC Design Synthesis Exercise integrates the complete aerospace design process; UCR optional independent research is comparison-only and does not reproduce that engineering capstone.

notes.text: The UCR programmes develop mathematical and computational models, autonomous systems, one general product-development project, natural-system analysis, resource recovery and renewable-energy assessment. They do not reproduce engineering mechanics, aerodynamics, aerospace structures and materials, propulsion, flight and orbital mechanics, aerospace control, wind-tunnel or flight-test practice, production engineering, integrated aircraft or spacecraft design, or the Design Synthesis Exercise.
